correctness.rationale: For any fully receptive state, direct expansion of the symmetric self-inclusive update gives x_i^+=mu+(c/n)g_i, with sum(g_i)=0 and |g_i|<=d_i. The top-two-degree bound gives strict universal preservation and the extremal rank ordering constructs a first-step failure when the bound is not strict. In the preserving regime, g is a subgradient of the convex hostile-edge total absolute difference Q. Phi=Q-(n/2c)||x-mu||^2 increases at least (n/2c)||x^+-x||^2, and all post-first states lie in a finite score lattice, so a fixed point is reached in at most min(2^m,product_i(d_i+1)) time steps. The standalone script independently compared 2,800 exact rational source-update cases and 231,388 exhaustive finite assertions plus 7,818 sampled assertions. Finite checks supplement, rather than replace, the all-n proof.

value.rationale: The model paper explicitly treats antagonistic opinion-driven confidence fragmentation and leaves broad convergence questions open. The all-size criterion requires only the two largest hostile degrees and exactly separates signed complete networks that guarantee no confidence-edge rupture from networks admitting an immediate rupture. The same side admits a constructive finite-step, quantized equilibrium classification with a universal bound, despite nontrivial changes in rank order. This is a structural network-level result, not an arbitrary small-graph enumeration or conventional positive-only averaging deduction.
